title: Subjective Spine Value: Efficient Evaluation of Spinal Function
summary:
Over a 24-month period, 28 patients per subgroup (juvenile scoliosis, adolescent scoliosis, congenital scoliosis, secondary scoliosis, degenerative scoliosis, asymptomatic individuals) will be prospectively enrolled in the study. Patients with scoliotic spinal deformities are identified and recruited through the spine outpatient clinics of the Center for Musculoskeletal Surgery (CMSC). Diagnoses are established independently of the study, following the standard procedures of the clinic/spine center based on patient history, clinical examination, and radiological assessment. Similarly, conservative or surgical treatments are conducted independently of the study. Alongside standard clinical and radiological diagnostics and treatment, the study collects PROMs and validated scores, including the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Core Outcome Measures Index for the back (COMI-back), Scoliosis Research Society Score (SRS-22r), and satisfaction with any previous surgery measured by a numerical rating scale. Additionally, the Subjective Spine Value (SSpV) is collected, allowing patients to provide a subjective assessment of their spinal function on a single scale. The SSpV enables patients to rate their spine's functionality as a percentage from 0 to 100%, where 100% represents the functional level of a healthy spine.

Data collection occurs as part of medically indicated treatment or via email, in line with the standard communication methods used, and does not influence any diagnostic or therapeutic decisions. Assessments are conducted preoperatively and in the postoperative period (2-4 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively), complemented by the existing assessment modalities of the spine center.
conditions: Scoliosis (juvenile scoliosis, adolescent scoliosis, congenital scoliosis, secondary scoliosis, degenerative scoliosis, asymptomatic subjects)

interventions.name:
Healthy Participants (No Scoliosis) as Control Group

Additional questionnaires in addition to the study-independent treatment according to the standard of the spine center (see section Primary endpoint).

Juvenile Scoliosis (Conservative Therapy)

Annual recording of the questionnaires in addition to the study-independent treatment according to the standard of the Spine Center (see section Primary endpoint).

Juvenile Scoliosis (Surgical Therapy)

The questionnaires (see section Primary endpoint) are evaluated preoperatively as well as during the postoperative course (2-4 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months and 1 year postoperatively).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scoliotic deformity of the spine
Exclusion criteria:
No consent from the patient or legal guardian possible
Inability to adequately answer questionnaire items (e.g., language barrier, patient’s age)
